Si446x Command/Property API Documentation

Interface Version: 1.0

Document Version: 1.0.3

Generated: Tue Dec 11 14:55:03 2012

Introduction

This document provides API descriptions for the commands and properties used to control and configure the part. The interface version tracks any functional changes to the API (command, property, field, enumeration, etc.). The documentation version tracks any text changes to the summary or description text of the API components.

The commands are listed in a summary table with links to command details. The properties are listed in a summary table with links to property details. The feature available column in the summary tables lists the firmware revision which first implemented the command or property.

An entry in the summary table will link to a details section, which contains a register view with fields. Clicking a field in the register view will auto-expand the corresponding field details. An up button in the field detail links back to the register view. Each register view title links back to the summary table entry. These hyper-links provide two-click access from top to bottom.

View Controls

Use these buttons to control the table and list view. For successful browser search, please click Global Expand button.


Press <F5> to reset your browser to default view. The field hyperlink navigation will fill the browser page history. Use the button below to quickly return to the master index page.


Command Summary

BOOT_COMMANDS
Number Name Summary Feature Available
0x02 POWER_UP Power-up device and mode selection. Modes include operational function. revB1B
COMMON_COMMANDS
Number Name Summary Feature Available
0x00 NOP No operation command. revB1B
0x01 PART_INFO Reports basic information about the device. revB1B
0x10 FUNC_INFO Returns the Function revision information of the device. revB1B
0x20 GET_INT_STATUS Returns the interrupt status of ALL the possible interrupt events (both STATUS and PENDING). Optionally, it may be used to clear latched (PENDING) interrupt events. revB1B
0x11 SET_PROPERTY Sets the value of a property. revB1B
0x12 GET_PROPERTY Retrieve a property's value. revB1B
0x15 FIFO_INFO Provides access to transmit and receive FIFO counts and reset. revB1B
0x13 GPIO_PIN_CFG Configures the gpio pins. revB1B
0x34 CHANGE_STATE Update state machine entries. revB1B
0x33 REQUEST_DEVICE_STATE Request current device state. revB1B
0x44 READ_CMD_BUFF Used to read CTS and the command response. revB1B
0x50 FRR_A_READ Reads the fast response registers starting with A. revB1B
0x51 FRR_B_READ Reads the fast response registers starting with B. revB1B
0x53 FRR_C_READ Reads the fast response registers starting with C. revB1B
0x57 FRR_D_READ Reads the fast response registers starting with D. revB1B
IR_CAL_COMMANDS
Number Name Summary Feature Available
0x17 IRCAL Image rejection calibration. revB1B
TX_COMMANDS
Number Name Summary Feature Available
0x31 START_TX Switches to TX state and starts packet transmission. revB1B
0x66 WRITE_TX_FIFO Writes the TX FIFO. revB1B
RX_COMMANDS
Number Name Summary Feature Available
0x22 GET_MODEM_STATUS Returns the interrupt status of the Modem Interrupt Group (both STATUS and PENDING). Optionally, it may be used to clear latched (PENDING) interrupt events. revB1B
0x16 PACKET_INFO Returns information about the last packet received and optionally overrides field length. revB1B
0x32 START_RX Switches to RX state. Command arguments are retained though sleep state, so these only need to be written when they change. revB1B
0x36 RX_HOP Hop to a new frequency while in RX. revB1B
0x77 READ_RX_FIFO Reads the RX FIFO. revB1B
ADVANCED_COMMANDS
Number Name Summary Feature Available
0x21 GET_PH_STATUS Returns the interrupt status of the Packet Handler Interrupt Group (both STATUS and PENDING). Optionally, it may be used to clear latched (PENDING) interrupt events. revB1B
0x23 GET_CHIP_STATUS Returns the interrupt status of the Chip Interrupt Group (both STATUS and PENDING). Optionally, it may be used to clear latched (PENDING) interrupt events. revB1B
0x18 PROTOCOL_CFG Sets the chip up for specified protocol. revB1B
0x14 GET_ADC_READING Performs and retrieve the results of possible ADC conversions. revB1B

Command Details

POWER_UP

  • Number: 0x02
  • Summary: Power-up device and mode selection. Modes include operational function.
  • Purpose:
    • Power-up the device with the specified function. Power-up is complete when the CTS bit is set. This command may take longer to set the CTS bit than other commands.
  • Argument Stream:

    • POWER_UP Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x02
    0x01 BOOT_OPTIONS PATCH 0 FUNC
    0x02 XTAL_OPTIONS 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 TCXO
    0x03 XO_FREQ XO_FREQ[31:24]
    0x04 XO_FREQ[23:16]
    0x05 XO_FREQ[15:8]
    0x06 XO_FREQ[7:0]

  • Reply Stream:

    • POWER_UP Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS

ARGUMENT FIELDS
BOOT_OPTIONS
  • PATCH
    • Description: Select patch mode.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Copy selected functional image from otp and boot device.
      • 1 = Indicates a patch has been applied. Validate patched image matches function selected and boot.
  • FUNC[5:0]
    • Description: Selects the boot function of the device.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 1 = Boot main application image.
XTAL_OPTIONS
  • TCXO
    • Description: Select if TCXO is in use.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = XTAL is not TCXO.
      • 1 = XTAL is TCXO.
XO_FREQ
  • XO_FREQ[31:0]
    • Description: Frequency of TCXO or external crystal oscillator in Hz. The default is 30000000 (30 MHz).
    • Type: U8
    • Min: 25000000
    • Max: 32000000
    • Default: 0

REPLY FIELDS
CTS
  • CTS[7:0]
    • Description: Clear to Send. Indicates that the previous command has completed
      execution and DATA[1..16] is valid. The next command may be sent.
    • Type: U8

NOP

  • Number: 0x00
  • Summary: No operation command.
  • Purpose:
    • Can be used to ensure communication with the device.
  • Argument Stream:

    • NOP Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x00

  • Reply Stream:

    • NOP Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS

ARGUMENT FIELDS

REPLY FIELDS
CTS
  • CTS[7:0]
    • Description: Clear to Send. Indicates that the previous command has completed
      execution and DATA[1..16] is valid. The next command may be sent.
    • Type: U8

PART_INFO

  • Number: 0x01
  • Summary: Reports basic information about the device.
  • Purpose:
    • Returns Part Number, Part Version, ROM ID, etc.
  • Argument Stream:

    • PART_INFO Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x01

  • Reply Stream:

    • PART_INFO Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS
    0x01 CHIPREV CHIPREV
    0x02 PART PART[15:8]
    0x03 PART[7:0]
    0x04 PBUILD PBUILD
    0x05 ID ID[15:8]
    0x06 ID[7:0]
    0x07 CUSTOMER CUSTOMER
    0x08 ROMID ROMID

ARGUMENT FIELDS

REPLY FIELDS
CTS
  • CTS[7:0]
    • Description: Clear to Send. Indicates that the previous command has completed
      execution and DATA[1..16] is valid. The next command may be sent.
    • Type: U8
CHIPREV
  • CHIPREV[7:0]
    • Description: Chip Mask Revision.
    • Type: U8
PART
  • PART[15:0]
    • Description: Part Number (e.g., si4461 will return - 0x4461).
    • Type: U16
PBUILD
  • PBUILD[7:0]
    • Description: Part Build.
    • Type: U8
ID
  • ID[15:0]
    • Description: Id.
    • Type: U16
CUSTOMER
  • CUSTOMER[7:0]
    • Description: Customer ID.
    • Type: U8
ROMID
  • ROMID[7:0]
    • Description: ROM Id.
    • Type: U8

FUNC_INFO

  • Number: 0x10
  • Summary: Returns the Function revision information of the device.
  • Purpose:
    • Return Function revision numbers for currently loaded functional mode firmware. Contrast with PART_INFO.
  • Argument Stream:

    • FUNC_INFO Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x10

  • Reply Stream:

    • FUNC_INFO Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS
    0x01 REVEXT REVEXT
    0x02 REVBRANCH REVBRANCH
    0x03 REVINT REVINT
    0x04 RESERVED X X X X X X X X
    0x05 X X X X X X X X
    0x06 FUNC FUNC

ARGUMENT FIELDS

REPLY FIELDS
CTS
  • CTS[7:0]
    • Description: Clear to Send. Indicates that the previous command has completed
      execution and DATA[1..16] is valid. The next command may be sent.
    • Type: U8
REVEXT
  • REVEXT[7:0]
    • Description: External revision number.
    • Type: U8
    • Min: 0
    • Max: 255
    • Default: 0
REVBRANCH
  • REVBRANCH[7:0]
    • Description: Branch revision number.
    • Type: U8
    • Min: 0
    • Max: 255
    • Default: 0
REVINT
  • REVINT[7:0]
    • Description: Internal revision number.
    • Type: U8
    • Min: 0
    • Max: 255
    • Default: 0
FUNC
  • FUNC[7:0]
    • Description: Current functional mode.
    • Type: U8

SET_PROPERTY

  • Number: 0x11
  • Summary: Sets the value of a property.
  • Purpose:
    • Sets a property common to one or more commands. These are similar to parameters for an API command but are not expected to change frequently and may be controlled by higher layers of the user's software. Setting some properties may not cause the device to take immediate action; however, the property will take affect once a command which uses it is issued.
  • Argument Stream:

    • SET_PROPERTY Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x11
    0x01 GROUP GROUP
    0x02 NUM_PROPS NUM_PROPS
    0x03 START_PROP START_PROP
    0x04 DATA0 DATA0
    0x05 DATA1 DATA1
    0x06 DATA2 DATA2
    0x07 DATA3 DATA3
    0x08 DATA4 DATA4
    0x09 DATA5 DATA5
    0x0a DATA6 DATA6
    0x0b DATA7 DATA7
    0x0c DATA8 DATA8
    0x0d DATA9 DATA9
    0x0e DATA10 DATA10
    0x0f DATA11 DATA11

  • Reply Stream:

    • SET_PROPERTY Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS

ARGUMENT FIELDS
GROUP
  • GROUP[7:0]
    • Description: Selects the group of the property to set.
    • Type: U8
NUM_PROPS
  • NUM_PROPS[7:0]
    • Description: Number of properties to write starting at START_PROP.
    • Type: U8
    • Min: 1
    • Max: 12
    • Default: 0
START_PROP
  • START_PROP[7:0]
    • Description: Selects the property index to set. The available properties are determined by the part number and the POWER_UP:FUNC selection.
    • Type: U8
DATA0
  • DATA0[7:0]
    • Description: Value of the property START_PROP.
    • Type: U8
DATA1
  • DATA1[7:0]
    • Description: Value of the property START_PROP + 1 (don't care if NUM_PROPS < 2).
    • Type: U8
DATA2
  • DATA2[7:0]
    • Description: Value of the property START_PROP + 2 (don't care if NUM_PROPS < 3).

GET_PROPERTY

  • Number: 0x12
  • Summary: Retrieve a property's value.
  • Purpose:
    • Retrieve a property's value. The value will either be the default or the value set with SET_PROPERTY.
  • Argument Stream:

    • GET_PROPERTY Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0

    0x01 GROUP GROUP
    0x02 NUM_PROPS NUM_PROPS

GPIO_PIN_CFG

  • Number: 0x13
  • Summary: Configures the gpio pins.
  • Purpose:
  • Argument Stream:

    • GPIO_PIN_CFG Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x13
    0x01 GPIO0 0 GPIO0_PULL_CTL GPIO0_MODE
    0x02 GPIO1 0 GPIO1_PULL_CTL GPIO1_MODE
    0x03 GPIO2 0 GPIO2_PULL_CTL GPIO2_MODE
    0x04 GPIO3 0 GPIO3_PULL_CTL GPIO3_MODE
    0x05 NIRQ 0 NIRQ_DRV_PULL NIRQ_MODE
    0x06 SDO 0 SDO_PULL_CTL SDO_MODE
    0x07 GEN_CONFIG 0 DRV_STRENGTH 0 0 0 0 0

  • Reply Stream:

    • GPIO_PIN_CFG Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS
    0x01 GPIO0 GPIO0_STATE X GPIO0R
    0x02 GPIO1 GPIO1_STATE X GPIO1R
    0x03 GPIO2 GPIO2_STATE X GPIO2R
    0x04 GPIO3 GPIO3STATE X GPIO3R
    0x05 NIRQ NIRQSTATE X NIRQR
    0x06 SDO SDOSTATE X SDOR
    0x07 GEN_CONFIG X DRV_STRENGTH X X X X X

ARGUMENT FIELDS
GPIO0
  • GPIO0_PULL_CTL
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Disable pullup. Recommended setting if pin is driven.
      • 1 = Enable pullup.
  • GPIO0_MODE[5:0]
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = DONOTHING - Do not modify the behavior of this pin.
      • 1 = TRISTATE - Input and output drivers disabled.
      • 2 = DRIVE0 - CMOS output driven low.
      • 3 = DRIVE1 - CMOS output driven high.
      • 4 = INPUT - CMOS input. This is used for all GPIO functions that require the pin to be an input (e.g., TX Direct Mode Data In). What this pin is used for is controlled by other properties.
      • 5 = 32K_CLK - Outputs 32 kHz clock selected using GLOBAL_CLK_CFG:CLK_32K_SEL. Output low if the 32 kHz clock is not enabled.
      • 6 = BOOT_CLK - Outputs boot clock. This will only output when the boot clock in SPI ACTIVE state because that is the only time the boot clock is active.
      • 7 = DIV_CLK - Outputs divided clock. Output divided boot clock in SPI ACTIVE state, Output low while in SLEEP state as the divided clock source is not running, and Output divided XTAL in all other states. The divider is configured using GLOBAL_CLK_CFG:DIVIDED_CLK_SEL.
      • 8 = CTS - Output High when clear to send a new command, output low otherwise.
      • 9 = INV_CTS - Output low when clear to send a new command, output high otherwise.
      • 10 = CMD_OVERLAP - Output low unless command overlap occurs. When command overlap occurs output goes high until the rising edge of CTS.
      • 11 = SDO - Output SPI Serial data out.
      • 12 = POR - Output low until power on reset is complete then output high.
      • 13 = CAL_WUT - Output low normally, Pulses high for one 32 kHz clock cycle when calibration timer expires. To use the calibration timer the 32 kHz clock must be enabled. Calibration timer period is configured using GLOBAL_WUT_CONFIG:WUT_CAL_PERIOD and enabled by GLOBAL_WUT_CONFIG:CAL_EN.
      • 14 = WUT - Output low normally, Pulses high for one 32 kHz clock cycle for when wakeup timer expires. To use the wakeup timer the 32 kHz clock must be enabled. The WUT period is configured using GLOBAL_WUT_M_15_8, GLOBAL_WUT_M_7_0, and GLOBAL_WUT_R and enabled by GLOBAL_WUT_CONFIG:WUT_EN.
      • 16 = TX_DATA_CLK - Outputs TX data CLK to be used in conjunction with TX Data pin.
      • 17 = RX_DATA_CLK - Outputs RX data CLK to be used in conjunction with RX Data pin.
      • 20 = RX_DATA - Outputs RX data.
      • 21 = RX_RAW_DATA - RX raw data.
      • 22 = ANTENNA_0_SW - Antenna 1 Switch used for antenna diversity.
      • 23 = ANTENNA_1_SW - Antenna 2 Switch used for antenna diversity.
      • 24 = VALID_PREAMBLE - Output high when a valid preamble is detected. Returns to output low after packet received or sync word timeout occurs.
      • 25 = INVALID_PREAMBLE - Output low normally, pulses output high when the preamble is not detected within a period time (determined by PREAMBLE_CONFIG_STD_2:RX_PREAMBLE_TIMEOUT) after the demodulator is enabled.
      • 26 = SYNC_WORD_DETECT - Output high when a sync word is detected. Returns to output low after the packet is received.
      • 27 = CCA - Output high when RSSI above clear channel assessment threshold set by MODEM_RSSI_THRESH. Output low when below threshold.
      • 32 = TX_STATE - Output high while in TX state. Output low otherwise.
      • 33 = RX_STATE - Output high while in RX state. Output low otherwise.
      • 34 = RX_FIFO_FULL - Output high while the RX FIFO is almost full. Output low otherwise.
      • 35 = TX_FIFO_EMPTY - Output high while the TX FIFO is almost empty. Output low otherwise.
      • 36 = LOW_BATT - Output high while the battery voltage is low. Output low otherwise.
      • 37 = CCA_LATCH - Output high if RSSI goes above clear channel assesment threshold. Returns to output low on sync detect or exiting RX state.
      • 38 = HOPPED - Toggles between output high and output low when hop occurs.
      • 39 = HOP_TABLE_WRAP - Toggles between output high and output low when the hop table wraps.

      • 27 = CCA - Output high when RSSI above clear channel assessment threshold set by MODEM_RSSI_THRESH. Output low when below threshold.
      • 32 = TX_STATE - Output high while in TX state. Output low otherwise.
      • 33 = RX_STATE - Output high while in RX state. Output low otherwise.
      • 34 = RX_FIFO_FULL - Output high while the RX FIFO is almost full. Output low otherwise.
      • 35 = TX_FIFO_EMPTY - Output high while the TX FIFO is almost empty. Output low otherwise.
      • 36 = LOW_BATT - Output high while the battery voltage is low. Output low otherwise.
      • 37 = CCA_LATCH - Output high if RSSI goes above clear channel assesment threshold. Returns to output low on sync detect or exiting RX state.
      • 38 = HOPPED - Toggles between output high and output low when hop occurs.
      • 39 = HOP_TABLE_WRAP - Toggles between output high and output low when the hop table wraps.

FIFO_INFO

  • Number: 0x15
  • Summary: Provides access to transmit and receive FIFO counts and reset.
  • Purpose:
    • This command is normally used for error recovery, FIFO hardware does not need to be reset prior to use.
  • Argument Stream:

    • FIFO_INFO Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x15
    0x01 FIFO 0 0 0 0 0 0 RX TX

  • Reply Stream:

    • FIFO_INFO Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS
    0x01 RX_FIFO_COUNT RX_FIFO_COUNT
    0x02 TX_FIFO_SPACE TX_FIFO_SPACE

ARGUMENT FIELDS
FIFO
  • RX
    • Description: Resets RX FIFO and RX FIFO mode specified in property GLOBAL_CONFIG will be effective after reset.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = No need to reset RX data FIFO.
      • 1 = Resets receive data FIFO.
  • TX
    • Description: Resets TX FIFO and TX FIFO mode specified in property GLOBAL_CONFIG will be effective after reset.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = No need to reset TX data FIFO.
      • 1 = Resets transmit data FIFO.

REPLY FIELDS
CTS
  • CTS[7:0]
    • Description: Clear to Send. Indicates that the previous command has completed
      execution and DATA[1..16] is valid. The next command may be sent.
    • Type: U8
RX_FIFO_COUNT
  • RX_FIFO_COUNT[7:0]
    • Type: U8
TX_FIFO_SPACE
  • TX_FIFO_SPACE[7:0]
    • Description: Amount of space currently available in transmit FIFO.
    • Type: U8

GET_INT_STATUS

  • Number: 0x20
  • Summary: Returns the interrupt status of ALL the possible interrupt events (both STATUS and PENDING). Optionally, it may be used to clear latched (PENDING) interrupt events.
  • Purpose:
    • Returns the current interrupt status of ALL the possible interrupt events (both STATUS and PENDING) and optionally clears PENDING interrupts.
    • STATUS indicates the current state of an internal interrupt event such as preamble/sync word detection, packet sent/received, etc. For example, PREAMBLE_DETECT is low before detection of a valid preamble, but goes high when the preamble arrives and is successfully detected. STATUS is cleared automatically upon termination or cessation of the corresponding internal interrupt event.
    • PENDING simply latches the rising edge of the corresponding STATUS, and does not change until cleared by a GET_INT_STATUS command (or GET_CHIP_STATUS, GET_PH_STATUS, GET_MODEM_STATUS). For example, PREAMBLE_DETECT_PEND is low before detection of a valid preamble, goes high with PREAMBLE_DETECT, and remains high until cleared.
    • It is possible to poll for interrupts by reading the STATUS and PENDING response bytes, as they are always up-to-date. Additionally, PENDING interrupts may generate a HW interrupt on the NIRQ output pin, if the interrupt is enabled via INT_CTL_ENABLE, INT_CTL_PH_ENABLE, INT_CTL_MODEM_ENABLE, and INT_CTL_CHIP_ENABLE properties.
    • Sending the GET_INT_STATUS command with NO input parameters results in clearing all of the PENDING interrupts.
    • When PENDING interrupts are being cleared, the reply stream reflects their status prior to clearing.
  • Argument Stream:

    • GET_INT_STATUS Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x20
    0x01 PH_CLR_PEND FILTER_MATCH_PEND_CLR FILTER_MISS_PEND_CLR PACKET_SENT_PEND_CLR PACKET_RX_PEND_CLR CRC_ERROR_PEND_CLR 0 TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY_PEND_CLR RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL_PEND_CLR
    0x02 MODEM_CLR_PEND 0 POSTAMBLE_DETECT_PEND_CLR INVALID_SYNC_PEND_CLR RSSI_JUMP_PEND_CLR RSSI_PEND_CLR INVALID_PREAMBLE_PEND_CLR PREAMBLE_DETECT_PEND_CLR SYNC_DETECT_PEND_CLR
    0x03 CHIP_CLR_PEND 0 CAL_PEND_CLR FIFO_UNDERFLOW_OVERFLOW_ERROR_PEND_CLR STATE_CHANGE_PEND_CLR CMD_ERROR_PEND_CLR CHIP_READY_PEND_CLR LOW_BATT_PEND_CLR WUT_PEND_CLR

  • Reply Stream:

    • GET_INT_STATUS Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS
    0x01 INT_PEND X X X X X CHIP_INT_PEND MODEM_INT_PEND PH_INT_PEND
    0x02 INT_STATUS X X X X X CHIP_INT_STATUS MODEM_INT_STATUS PH_INT_STATUS
    0x03 PH_PEND FILTER_MATCH_PEND FILTER_MISS_PEND PACKET_SENT_PEND PACKET_RX_PEND CRC_ERROR_PEND X TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY_PEND RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL_PEND
    0x04 PH_STATUS FILTER_MATCH FILTER_MISS PACKET_SENT PACKET_RX CRC_ERROR X TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL
    0x05 MODEM_PEND X POSTAMBLE_DETECT_PEND INVALID_SYNC_PEND RSSI_JUMP_PEND RSSI_PEND INVALID_PREAMBLE_PEND PREAMBLE_DETECT_PEND SYNC_DETECT_PEND
    0x06 MODEM_STATUS X POSTAMBLE_DETECT INVALID_SYNC RSSI_JUMP RSSI INVALID_PREAMBLE PREAMBLE_DETECT SYNC_DETECT
    0x07 CHIP_PEND X CAL_PEND FIFO_UNDERFLOW_OVERFLOW_ERROR_PEND STATE_CHANGE_PEND CMD_ERROR_PEND CHIP_READY_PEND LOW_BATT_PEND WUT_PEND
    0x08 CHIP_STATUS X CAL FIFO_UNDERFLOW_OVERFLOW_ERROR STATE_CHANGE CMD_ERROR CHIP_READY LOW_BATT WUT

  • CHIP_INT_PEND
    • Description: If set, an enabled CHIP_PEND bit is set indicating an interrupt is pending. See the CHIP_STATUS field for the triggering events within the Chip Interrupt group.
    • Type: U8
  • MODEM_INT_PEND
    • Description: If set, an enabled MODEM_PEND bit is set indicating an interrupt is pending. See the MODEM_STATUS field for the triggering events within the Modem Interrupt group.
    • Type: U8
  • PH_INT_PEND
    • Description: If set, an enabled PH_PEND bit is set indicating an interrupt is pending. See the PH_STATUS field for the triggering events within the Packet Handler Interrupt group.
    • Type: U8
INT_STATUS
  • CHIP_INT_STATUS
    • Description: If set, the Chip Status Interrupt group has an interrupt pending. See the PH_PEND field for the triggering events within the Chip Status Interrupt group.
    • Type: U8
  • MODEM_INT_STATUS
    • Description: If set, the Modem Interrupt group has an interrupt pending. See the PH_PEND field for the triggering events within the Modem Interrupt group.
    • Type: U8
  • PH_INT_STATUS
    • Description: If set, the Packet Handler Interrupt group has an interrupt pending. See the PH_PEND field for the triggering events within the Packet Handler Interrupt group.
    • Type: U8
PH_PEND
  • FILTER_MATCH_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the FILTER_MATCH status bit has been detected and therefore a FILTER_MATCH interrupt is pending. See associated FILTER_MATCH status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • FILTER_MISS_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the FILTER_MISS status bit has been detected and therefore a FILTER_MISS interrupt is pending. See associated FILTER_MISS status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • PACKET_SENT_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the PACKET_SENT status bit has been detected and therefore a PACKET_SENT interrupt is pending. See associated PACKET_SENT status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • PACKET_RX_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the PACKET_RX status bit has been detected and therefore a PACKET_RX interrupt is pending. See associated PACKET_RX status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • CRC_ERROR_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the CRC_ERROR status bit has been detected and therefore a CRC_ERROR interrupt is pending. See associated CRC_ERROR status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY status bit has been detected and therefore a TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY interrupt is pending. See associated TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL status bit has been detected and therefore a RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL interrupt is pending. See associated RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
PH_STATUS
  • FILTER_MATCH
    • Description: Set to indicate the incoming packet matched filter. Cleared upon entry into RX state, or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • FILTER_MISS
    • Description: Set to indicate the incoming packet was discarded because filter did not match. Cleared upon entry into RX state, or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • PACKET_SENT
    • Description: Set to indicate that data bytes in the TX FIFO were transmitted successfully. Cleared upon entry into TX state.
    • Type: U8
  • PACKET_RX
    • Description: Set to indicate that the expected number of data bytes have been successfully received and placed in the RX FIFO. All enabled Packet Handler functions (e.g., CRC check, Filter Matching) must be successfully completed in order to generate a PACKET_RX interrupt.
    • Type: U8
  • CRC_ERROR
    • Description: Set to indicate that the received CRC checksum byte(s) do not match the calculated CRC checksum value. Cleared upon entry into RX state or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY
    • Description: Set to indicate that the amount of space in the TX FIFO is equal to or greater than the PKT_TX_THRESHOLD value. This interrupt may be used to signal the host MCU to store more data bytes into the TX FIFO, thus providing a means for handling packets with lengths greater than the size of the TX FIFO (i.e., 64 bytes, or 129 bytes in shared FIFO mode). Cleared if the amount of data in the TX FIFO is less than the PKT_TX_THRESHOLD value.
    • Type: U8
  • RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL
    • Description: Set to indicate that the number of bytes stored in the RX FIFO is equal to or greater than the PKT_RX_THRESHOLD value. This interrupt may be used to signal the host MCU to read more data bytes from the RX FIFO, thus providing a means for handling packets with lengths greater than the size of the RX FIFO (i.e., 64 bytes, or 129 bytes in shared FIFO mode). Cleared if the amount of data in the RX FIFO is less than the PKT_TX_THRESHOLD value.
    • Type: U8
MODEM_PEND
  • POSTAMBLE_DETECT_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the POSTAMBLE_DETECT status bit has been detected and therefore a POSTAMBLE_DETECT interrupt is pending. See associated POSTAMBLE_DETECT status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • INVALID_SYNC_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the INVALID_SYNC status bit has been detected and therefore a INVALID_SYNC interrupt is pending. See associated INVALID_SYNC status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • RSSI_JUMP_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the RSSI_JUMP status bit has been detected and therefore a RSSI_JUMP interrupt is pending. See associated RSSI_JUMP status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • RSSI_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the RSSI status bit has been detected and therefore a RSSI interrupt is pending. See associated RSSI status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • INVALID_PREAMBLE_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the INVALID_PREAMBLE status bit has been detected and therefore a INVALID_PREAMBLE interrupt is pending. See associated INVALID_PREAMBLE status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • PREAMBLE_DETECT_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the PREAMBLE_DETECT status bit has been detected and therefore a PREAMBLE_DETECT interrupt is pending. See associated PREAMBLE_DETECT status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • SYNC_DETECT_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the SYNC_DETECT status bit has been detected and therefore a SYNC_DETECT interrupt is pending. See associated SYNC_DETECT status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
MODEM_STATUS
  • POSTAMBLE_DETECT
    • Description: Set if 1-4 bytes of received data matches the pattern of bits defined in the POSTAMBLE_PATTERN_XX properties. Postamble detection must also be enabled in the PREAMBLE_POSTAMBLE_CONFIG property. Cleared upon entry into RX, or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • INVALID_SYNC
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high when a valid Sync Word (matching the pattern of bits defined in the SYNC_BITS_XX properties) was not detected within the allowed search timeout period. If configured to receive a standard preamble, the search timeout period is Sync Word Length + 4bits. If configured to receive a non-standard preamble, the search timeout period is defined by the PREAMBLE_TX_LENGTH property.
    • Type: U8
  • RSSI_JUMP
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high when the Current RSSI value jumps by more than the threshold value defined in the MODEM_RSSI_JUMP_THRESH property.
    • Type: U8
  • RSSI
    • Description: Set if the current RSSI value has exceeded the threshold value defined in the MODEM_RSSI_THRESH property. Cleared upon entry into RX state or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • INVALID_PREAMBLE
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high indicating that one of the following has occurred: a) a valid Preamble was not detected within the allowed search timeout period, or b) the Latched RSSI value is below the MODEM_RSSI_THRESH value and the chip has been enabled to check for this condition. The search timeout period for Preamble is configured in PREAMBLE_CONFIG_STD_2, while the CHECK_THRESH_AT_LATCH function is configured in MODEM_RSSI_CONTROL.
    • Type: U8
  • PREAMBLE_DETECT
    • Description: Set when a pattern of bits was received that matched the expected Preamble pattern. If configured to receive a standard preamble, the expected pattern of bits is '...010101...' with a threshold length defined in PREAMBLE_CONFIG_STD_1. If configured to receive a non-standard preamble, the expected pattern of bits is defined by the PREAMBLE_PATTERN_XX and the PREAMBLE_CONFIG_NSTD properties. Cleared when SYNC is detected, upon entering RX state, or RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • SYNC_DETECT
    • Description: Set when the received Sync Word pattern matched the pattern of bits defined in the SYNC_BITS_XX properties. Cleared when a packet is received (valid or invalid), upon entry into RX state, or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
CHIP_PEND
  • CAL_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the CAL status bit has been detected and therefore a CAL interrupt is pending. See associated CAL status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • FIFO_UNDERFLOW_OVERFLOW_ERROR_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the FIFO_UNDERFLOW_OVERFLOW_ERROR status bit has been detected and therefore a FIFO_UNDERFLOW_OVERFLOW_ERROR interrupt is pending. See associated FIFO_UNDERFLOW_OVERFLOW_ERROR status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • STATE_CHANGE_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the STATE_CHANGE status bit has been detected and therefore a STATE_CHANGE interrupt is pending. See associated STATE_CHANGE status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • CMD_ERROR_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the CMD_ERROR status bit has been detected and therefore a CMD_ERROR interrupt is pending. See associated CMD_ERROR status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • CHIP_READY_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the CHIP_READY status bit has been detected and therefore a CHIP_READY interrupt is pending. See associated CHIP_READY status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • LOW_BATT_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the LOW_BATT status bit has been detected and therefore a LOW_BATT interrupt is pending. See associated LOW_BATT status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • WUT_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the WUT status bit has been detected and therefore a WUT interrupt is pending. See associated WUT status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
CHIP_STATUS
  • CAL
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high to indicate a RC32K calibration event is pending. If this occurs, the RC32K oscillator will be calibrated on the next transition to Sleep/Standby state.
    • Type: U8
  • FIFO_UNDERFLOW_OVERFLOW_ERROR
    • Description: Set to indicate that the number of received or transmitted bytes exceeds the size of the RX or TX FIFO, respectively (i.e., 64 bytes for each FIFO, or 129 bytes when sharing the FIFO). Upon such an underflow/overflow event, the FIFO(s) will need to be reset. Cleared by issuing a FIFO_INFO command to reset the FIFOs.
    • Type: U8
  • STATE_CHANGE
    • Description: Set to indicate a successful transition from one state to another operating state. Cleared when a state transition is in progress.
    • Type: U8
  • CMD_ERROR
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high to indicate an error has occurred in the processing of a command. For example, an incorrect command/property ID is sent, or an attempt was made to write a property that is outside of the given property group.
    • Type: U8
  • CHIP_READY
    • Description: Set to indicate the chip (upon completion of the POWER_UP sequence) has reached the state where it is ready to accept commands, or when the IR calibration process is completed. Cleared when the chip is shutdown or when IR calibration has begun.
    • Type: U8
  • LOW_BATT
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high to indicate the WUT (Wake-up timer) has expired.
    • Type: U8
  • WUT
    • Description: Set to indicate the battery voltage is below the threshold set by GLOBAL_LOW_BATT_THRESH. Cleared to indicate the battery voltage is above the threshold set by GLOBAL_LOW_BATT_THRESH.
    • Type: U8

REQUEST_DEVICE_STATE

  • Number: 0x33
  • Summary: Request current device state.
  • Purpose:
    • Requests the current state of the device.
  • Argument Stream:

    • REQUEST_DEVICE_STATE Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x33

  • Reply Stream:

    • REQUEST_DEVICE_STATE Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS
    0x01 CURR_STATE X X X X MAIN_STATE
    0x02 CURRENT_CHANNEL CURRENT_CHANNEL

ARGUMENT FIELDS

REPLY FIELDS
CTS
  • CTS[7:0]
    • Description: Clear to Send. Indicates that the previous command has completed
      execution and DATA[1..16] is valid. The next command may be sent.
    • Type: U8
CURR_STATE
  • MAIN_STATE[3:0]
    • Description: Current State.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 1 = Sleep/Standby state. RC32K operation in this state is controlled using GLOBAL_CLK_CFG:CLK_32K_SEL.
      • 2 = SPI Active state.
      • 3 = Ready state.
      • 4 = Another enumeration for Ready state.
      • 5 = Tune state for TX.
      • 6 = Tune state for RX.
      • 7 = TX state.
      • 8 = RX state.
CURRENT_CHANNEL
  • CURRENT_CHANNEL[7:0]
    • Type: U8

IRCAL

  • Number: 0x17
  • Summary: Image rejection calibration.
  • Purpose:
    • Performs image rejection calibration. Completion can be monitored by polling CTS or waiting for CHIP_READY interrupt source.
  • Argument Stream:

    • IRCAL Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x17
    0x01 SEARCHING_STEP_SIZE 0 INITIAL_PH_AMP FINE_STEP_SIZE COARSE_STEP_SIZE
    0x02 SEARCHING_RSSI_AVG 0 0 RSSI_FINE_AVG 0 0 RSSI_COARSE_AVG
    0x03 RX_CHAIN_SETTING1 EN_HRMNIC_GEN IRCLKDIV RF_SOURCE_PWR CLOSE_SHUNT_SWITCH PGA_GAIN
    0x04 RX_CHAIN_SETTING2 0000 0 0 0 ADC_HIGH_GAIN

  • Reply Stream:

    • IRCAL Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS

ARGUMENT FIELDS
SEARCHING_STEP_SIZE
  • INITIAL_PH_AMP
    • Description: Initial ph and amp value when start IR calibration.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 1 = Use zero for phase and amplitude values as starting values.
      • 0 = Use previous calibration values as starting values.
  • FINE_STEP_SIZE[1:0]
    • Description: Step size of fine stepping. Writing a value of 0 will skip fine stepping.
    • Type: U8
  • COARSE_STEP_SIZE[3:0]
    • Description: Step Size of coarse stepping. Writing a value of 0 will skip coarse stepping.
    • Type: U8
SEARCHING_RSSI_AVG
  • RSSI_FINE_AVG[1:0]
    • Description: How many measurements(2^avg) per RSSI measurement while fine stepping.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = 1 measurement.
      • 1 = 2 measurements.
      • 2 = 4 measurements.
      • 3 = 8 measurements.
  • RSSI_COARSE_AVG[1:0]
    • Description: How many measurements(2^avg) per RSSI measurement while coarse stepping.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = 1 measurement.
      • 1 = 2 measurements.
      • 2 = 4 measurements.

START_TX

  • Number: 0x31
  • Summary: Switches to TX state and starts packet transmission.
  • Purpose:
    • Switches to TX state when condition is met. Command arguments are retained though sleep state, so they only need to be written when they change. CTS will not return high until in TX state.
  • Argument Stream:

    • START_TX Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x31
    0x01 CHANNEL CHANNEL
    0x02 CONDITION TXCOMPLETE_STATE 0 RETRANSMIT START
    0x03 TX_LEN TX_LEN[15:8]
    0x04 TX_LEN[7:0]
    0x05 TX_DELAY TX_DELAY

  • Reply Stream:

    • START_TX Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS

ARGUMENT FIELDS
CHANNEL
  • CHANNEL[7:0]
    • Description: Channel number to tune the receiver to. Frequency is determined using integer, fractional, and step size properties in the FREQ_CONTROL property group. This value will be overwritten with START_RX:CHANNEL if supported.
    • Type: U8
    • Min: 0
    • Max: 255
    • Default: 0
CONDITION
  • TXCOMPLETE_STATE[3:0]
    • Description: State to go to when current packet transmission completes. If this parameter is not sent with the command, the last value specified is used. Defaults to 3.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Do not change from previously sent TXCOMPLETE_STATE.
      • 1 = Sleep/Standby state. RC32K operation in this state is controlled using GLOBAL_CLK_CFG:CLK_32K_SEL.
      • 2 = SPI Active state.
      • 3 = Ready state.
      • 4 = Another enumeration for Ready state.
      • 5 = Tune state for TX.
      • 6 = Tune state for RX.
      • 7 = TX state.
      • 8 = RX state.
  • RETRANSMIT
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Send data that has been written to FIFO. If FIFO is empty a FIFO underflow interrupt will occur.
      • 1 = Send last packet again. If this option is used, ensure that no new data is written to the FIFO.
  • START[1:0]
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Start TX immediately.
      • 1 = Start TX when wake up timer expires.
      • 3 = Update TX parameters.
TX_LEN
  • TX_LEN[15:0]
    • Description: If this field is nonzero, the packet will be transmitted using only field 1. If this field is zero, the configuration of the packet handler fields is used. If RETRANSMIT is set, this field is ignored.
    • Type: U8
    • Min: 0
    • Max: 8191
    • Default: 0
TX_DELAY
  • TX_DELAY[7:0]
    • Description: Delay in us between transmits if another transmit is scheduled.
    • Type: U8
    • Min: 0
    • Max: 128
    • Default: 0

REPLY FIELDS
CTS
  • CTS[7:0]
    • Description: Clear to Send. Indicates that the previous command has completed
      execution and DATA[1..16] is valid. The next command may be sent.
    • Type: U8

WRITE_TX_FIFO

  • Number: 0x66
  • Summary: Writes the TX FIFO.
  • Purpose:
    • This command does not cause CTS to go low, and can be sent and the reply read while CTS is low.

      This command has no response to be read.
      If you write more data than the TX FIFO can hold it will trigger a FIFO Overflow interrupt.
  • Argument Stream:

    • WRITE_TX_FIFO Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x66
    0x01 FIRST_BYTE FIRST_BYTE


ARGUMENT FIELDS
FIRST_BYTE
  • FIRST_BYTE[7:0]
    • Description: First byte to write to the TX FIFO.
    • Type: U8

PACKET_INFO

  • Number: 0x16
  • Summary: Returns information about the last packet received and optionally overrides field length.
  • Purpose:
    • This command is used to retrieve the length field extracted from the packet when using variable length packets.
    • On 802.15.4g receive mode, the FCS byte length embedded in the FHR is included to inform the host of the number of FCS bytes in the FIFO following the MAC Payload. if FCS is 0, 2 is added to the return length; if FCS is 1, 4 is added to the return length.
    • If arguments follow, it can also be used to override packet length that was originally programmed with non-zero RX_LEN in START_RX or field length originally programmed with PKT field length properties.
  • Argument Stream:

    • PACKET_INFO Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x16
    0x01 FIELD_NUMBER 0 0 0 FIELD_NUM
    0x02 LEN LEN[15:8]
    0x03 LEN[7:0]
    0x04 LEN_DIFF LEN_DIFF[15:8]
    0x05 LEN_DIFF[7:0]

  • Reply Stream:

    • PACKET_INFO Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS
    0x01 LENGTH_15_8 LENGTH_15_8
    0x02 LENGTH_7_0 LENGTH_7_0

ARGUMENT FIELDS
FIELD_NUMBER
  • FIELD_NUM[4:0]
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Nothing to override.
      • 1 = Override FIELD 1 length or RX_LEN in START_RX.
      • 2 = Override FIELD 2 length.
      • 4 = Override FIELD 3 length.
      • 8 = Override FIELD 4 length.
      • 16 = Override FIELD 5 length.
LEN
  • LEN[15:0]
    • Description: Length in bytes.
    • Type: U8
    • Min: 1
    • Max: 8191
    • Default: 0
LEN_DIFF
  • LEN_DIFF[15:0]
    • Description: Difference in bytes based on the original field length or RX_LEN. Signed.
    • Type: S16
    • Min: -32768
    • Max: 32767
    • Default: 0

REPLY FIELDS
CTS
  • CTS[7:0]
    • Description: Clear to Send. Indicates that the previous command has completed
      execution and DATA[1..16] is valid. The next command may be sent.
    • Type: U8
LENGTH_15_8
  • LENGTH_15_8[7:0]
    • Description: Most significant byte of the extracted length.
    • Type: U8
LENGTH_7_0
  • LENGTH_7_0[7:0]
    • Description: Least significant byte of the extracted length.
    • Type: U8

GET_MODEM_STATUS

  • Number: 0x22
  • Summary: Returns the interrupt status of the Modem Interrupt Group (both STATUS and PENDING). Optionally, it may be used to clear latched (PENDING) interrupt events.
  • Purpose:
    • Returns the current interrupt status of Modem interrupt events (both STATUS and PENDING) and optionally clears PENDING interrupts.
    • Please refer to the GET_INT_STATUS command for more details regarding the difference between STATUS and PENDING interrupts.
    • Sending the GET_MODEM_STATUS command with NO input parameter results in clearing all of the PENDING interrupts.
    • When PENDING interrupts are being cleared, the reply stream reflects their status prior to clearing.
  • Argument Stream:

    • GET_MODEM_STATUS Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x22
    0x01 MODEM_CLR_PEND 0 POSTAMBLE_DETECT_PEND_CLR INVALID_SYNC_PEND_CLR RSSI_JUMP_PEND_CLR RSSI_PEND_CLR INVALID_PREAMBLE_PEND_CLR PREAMBLE_DETECT_PEND_CLR SYNC_DETECT_PEND_CLR

  • Reply Stream:

    • GET_MODEM_STATUS Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS
    0x01 MODEM_PEND X POSTAMBLE_DETECT_PEND INVALID_SYNC_PEND RSSI_JUMP_PEND RSSI_PEND INVALID_PREAMBLE_PEND PREAMBLE_DETECT_PEND SYNC_DETECT_PEND
    0x02 MODEM_STATUS X POSTAMBLE_DETECT INVALID_SYNC RSSI_JUMP RSSI INVALID_PREAMBLE PREAMBLE_DETECT SYNC_DETECT
    0x03 CURR_RSSI CURR_RSSI
    0x04 LATCH_RSSI LATCH_RSSI
    0x05 ANT1_RSSI ANT1_RSSI
    0x06 ANT2_RSSI ANT2_RSSI
    0x07 AFC_FREQ_OFFSET AFC_FREQ_OFFSET[15:8]
    0x08 AFC_FREQ_OFFSET[7:0]

ARGUMENT FIELDS
MODEM_CLR_PEND
  • POSTAMBLE_DETECT_PEND_CLR
    • Description: If clear, Clear any pending POSTAMBLE_DETECT interrupt. If set, leave interrupt pending.
    • Type: U8
  • INVALID_SYNC_PEND_CLR
    • Description: If clear, Clear any pending INVALID_SYNC interrupt. If set, leave interrupt pending.
    • Type: U8
  • RSSI_JUMP_PEND_CLR
    • Description: If clear, Clear any pending RSSI_JUMP interrupt. If set, leave interrupt pending.
    • Type: U8
  • RSSI_PEND_CLR
    • Description: If clear, Clear any pending RSSI interrupt. If set, leave interrupt pending.
    • Type: U8
  • INVALID_PREAMBLE_PEND_CLR
    • Description: If clear, Clear any pending INVALID_PREAMBLE interrupt. If set, leave interrupt pending.
    • Type: U8
  • PREAMBLE_DETECT_PEND_CLR
    • Description: If clear, Clear any pending PREAMBLE_DETECT interrupt. If set, leave interrupt pending.
    • Type: U8
  • SYNC_DETECT_PEND_CLR
    • Description: If clear, Clear any pending SYNC_DETECT interrupt. If set, leave interrupt pending.
    • Type: U8

REPLY FIELDS
CTS
  • CTS[7:0]
    • Description: Clear to Send. Indicates that the previous command has completed
      execution and DATA[1..16] is valid. The next command may be sent.
    • Type: U8
MODEM_PEND
  • POSTAMBLE_DETECT_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the POSTAMBLE_DETECT status bit has been detected and therefore a POSTAMBLE_DETECT interrupt is pending. See associated POSTAMBLE_DETECT status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • INVALID_SYNC_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the INVALID_SYNC status bit has been detected and therefore a INVALID_SYNC interrupt is pending. See associated INVALID_SYNC status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • RSSI_JUMP_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the RSSI_JUMP status bit has been detected and therefore a RSSI_JUMP interrupt is pending. See associated RSSI_JUMP status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • RSSI_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the RSSI status bit has been detected and therefore a RSSI interrupt is pending. See associated RSSI status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • INVALID_PREAMBLE_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the INVALID_PREAMBLE status bit has been detected and therefore a INVALID_PREAMBLE interrupt is pending. See associated INVALID_PREAMBLE status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • PREAMBLE_DETECT_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the PREAMBLE_DETECT status bit has been detected and therefore a PREAMBLE_DETECT interrupt is pending. See associated PREAMBLE_DETECT status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • SYNC_DETECT_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the SYNC_DETECT status bit has been detected and therefore a SYNC_DETECT interrupt is pending. See associated SYNC_DETECT status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
MODEM_STATUS
  • POSTAMBLE_DETECT
    • Description: Set if 1-4 bytes of received data matches the pattern of bits defined in the POSTAMBLE_PATTERN_XX properties. Postamble detection must also be enabled in the PREAMBLE_POSTAMBLE_CONFIG property. Cleared upon entry into RX, or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • INVALID_SYNC
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high when a valid Sync Word (matching the pattern of bits defined in the SYNC_BITS_XX properties) was not detected within the allowed search timeout period. If configured to receive a standard preamble, the search timeout period is Sync Word Length + 4bits. If configured to receive a non-standard preamble, the search timeout period is defined by the PREAMBLE_TX_LENGTH property.
    • Type: U8
  • RSSI_JUMP
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high when the Current RSSI value jumps by more than the threshold value defined in the MODEM_RSSI_JUMP_THRESH property.
    • Type: U8
  • RSSI
    • Description: Set if the current RSSI value has exceeded the threshold value defined in the MODEM_RSSI_THRESH property. Cleared upon entry into RX state or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • INVALID_PREAMBLE
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high indicating that one of the following has occurred: a) a valid Preamble was not detected within the allowed search timeout period, or b) the Latched RSSI value is below the MODEM_RSSI_THRESH value and the chip has been enabled to check for this condition. The search timeout period for Preamble is configured in PREAMBLE_CONFIG_STD_2, while the CHECK_THRESH_AT_LATCH function is configured in MODEM_RSSI_CONTROL.
    • Type: U8
  • PREAMBLE_DETECT
    • Description: Set when a pattern of bits was received that matched the expected Preamble pattern. If configured to receive a standard preamble, the expected pattern of bits is '...010101...' with a threshold length defined in PREAMBLE_CONFIG_STD_1. If configured to receive a non-standard preamble, the expected pattern of bits is defined by the PREAMBLE_PATTERN_XX and the PREAMBLE_CONFIG_NSTD properties. Cleared when SYNC is detected, upon entering RX state, or RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • SYNC_DETECT
    • Description: Set when the received Sync Word pattern matched the pattern of bits defined in the SYNC_BITS_XX properties. Cleared when a packet is received (valid or invalid), upon entry into RX state, or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
CURR_RSSI
  • CURR_RSSI[7:0]
    • Description: Current RSSI reading from the modem.
    • Type: U8
LATCH_RSSI
  • LATCH_RSSI[7:0]
    • Description: Latched RSSI reading from the modem as configured by MODEM_RSSI_CONTROL. Reset to 0 upon entering RX mode or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
ANT1_RSSI
  • ANT1_RSSI[7:0]
    • Description: RSSI of ANT1 during evaluation of the antenna diversity algorithm. The RSSI value is latched during Preamble evaluation and is available for reading only after detection of Sync Word.
    • Type: U8
ANT2_RSSI
  • ANT2_RSSI[7:0]
    • Description: RSSI of ANT2 during evaluation of the antenna diversity algorithm. The RSSI value is latched during Preamble evaluation and is available for reading only after detection of Sync Word.
    • Type: U8
AFC_FREQ_OFFSET
  • AFC_FREQ_OFFSET[15:0]
    • Description: The AFC value that is generated by the PLL AFC feedback loop during receive mode.
    • Type: U16

  • Number: 0x32

    • START_RX Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x32
    0x01 CHANNEL CHANNEL
    0x02 CONDITION 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 START

ARGUMENT FIELDS
CHANNEL
  • CHANNEL[7:0]
    • Description: Channel number to transmit the packet on. Frequency is determined using integer, fractional, and step size properties in the FREQ_CONTROL property group. This value will be overwritten with START_TX:CHANNEL if supported.
    • Type: U8
    • Min: 0
    • Max: 255
    • Default: 0
CONDITION
  • START
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Start RX immediately.
      • 1 = Start RX when wake up timer expires.
RX_LEN
  • RX_LEN[15:0]
    • Description: If this field is nonzero, the packet will be received using only field 1. If this field is zero, the configuration of the packet handler fields is used.
    • Type: U8
    • Min: 0
    • Max: 8191
    • Default: 0
NEXT_STATE1
  • RXTIMEOUT_STATE[3:0]
    • Description: If preamble detection times out, RX will transition to RXTIMEOUT_STATE. See PREAMBLE_CONFIG_STD_2 for details regarding how to configure preamble timeout. Defaults to 0.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Remain in RX state if RXTIMEOUT occurs.
      • 1 = Sleep/Standby state. RC32K operation in this state is controlled using GLOBAL_CLK_CFG:CLK_32K_SEL.
      • 2 = SPI Active state.
      • 3 = Ready state.
      • 4 = Another enumeration for Ready state.
      • 5 = Tune state for TX.
      • 6 = Tune state for RX.
      • 7 = TX state.
      • 8 = RX state.
NEXT_STATE2
  • RXVALID_STATE[3:0]
    • Description: RX transitions to RXVALID_STATE if CRC check passes when CRC is enabled via PKT group properties. If CRC is not enabled, upon receiving packet received interrupt, RX transitions to RXVALID_STATE. Defaults to 3.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 1 = Sleep/Standby state. RC32K operation in this state is controlled using GLOBAL_CLK_CFG:CLK_32K_SEL.
      • 2 = SPI Active state.
      • 3 = Ready state.
      • 4 = Another enumeration for Ready state.
      • 5 = Tune state for TX.
      • 6 = Tune state for RX.
      • 7 = TX state.
      • 8 = RX state.
NEXT_STATE3
  • RXINVALID_STATE[3:0]
    • Description: If CRC checking is enabled, in case of CRC error, RX will transition to RXINVALID_STATE. Defaults to 3.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 1 = Sleep/Standby state. RC32K operation in this state is controlled using GLOBAL_CLK_CFG:CLK_32K_SEL.
      • 2 = Spi Active state.
      • 3 = Ready state.
      • 4 = Another enumeration for Ready state.
      • 5 = Tune state for TX.
      • 6 = Tune state for RX.
      • 7 = TX state.
      • 8 = RX state.

ARGUMENT FIELDS
ADC_EN
  • TEMPERATURE_EN
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Don't do ADC conversion of temperature, will read 0 value in reply TEMPERATURE.
      • 1 = Do ADC conversion of temperature, result in TEMP_ADC. Temp in Celsius = ((800 + TEMP_SLOPE)/4096)*TEMP_ADC - (INTERCEPT/2 + 256)
  • BATTERY_VOLTAGE_EN
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Don't do ADC conversion of battery voltage, will read 0 value in reply BATTERY_ADC.
      • 1 = Do ADC conversion of battery voltage, results in BATTERY_ADC. Vbatt = 3*BATTERY_ADC/1280
  • ADC_GPIO_EN
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Don't do ADC conversion on GPIO, will read 0 value in reply.
      • 1 = Do ADC conversion of GPIO, results in GPIO_ADC. Vgpio = GPIO_ADC/GPIO_ADC_DIV where GPIO_ADC_DIV is defined by GPIO_ATT selection.
  • ADC_GPIO_PIN[1:0]
    • Description: Select GPIOx pin. The pin must be set as input.

      • 1 = Measure voltage of GPIO1.
      • 2 = Measure voltage of GPIO2.
      • 3 = Measure voltage of GPIO3.
ADC_CFG
  • UDTIME[3:0]
    • Description: ADC conversion Time = SYS_CLK / 12 / 2^(UDTIME + 1). Defaults to 0xC if ADC_CFG is 0. Selecting shorter conversion times will result in lower ADC resolution and longer times will result in higher ADC resolution.
    • Type: U8
  • GPIO_ATT[3:0]
    • Description: Sets attenuation of gpio input voltage when vgpio measured. Defaults to 0xC if ADC_CFG is 0.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = ADC range 0 to 0.8 V. GPIO_ADC_DIV = 2560.
      • 4 = ADC range 0 to 1.6 V. GPIO_ADC_DIV = 1280.
      • 8 = ADC range 0 to 2.4 V. GPIO_ADC_DIV = 853.33.
      • 12 = ADC range 0 to 3.2 V. GPIO_ADC_DIV = 640.
      • 9 = ADC range 0 to 3.6 V. GPIO_ADC_DIV = 426.66.

PROTOCOL_CFG

  • Number: 0x18
  • Summary: Sets the chip up for specified protocol.
  • Purpose:
  • Argument Stream:

    • PROTOCOL_CFG Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x18
    0x01 PROTOCOL PROTOCOL

  • Reply Stream:

    • PROTOCOL_CFG Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS

ARGUMENT FIELDS
PROTOCOL
  • PROTOCOL[7:0]
    • Description: Selects which protocol to configure the chip for.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Packet format is generic, no dynamic reprogramming of packet handler properties.
      • 1 = Packet format is IEEE802.15.4g compliant. The following properties are overriden: PKT_CRC_CONFIG, CRC_ENDIAN/BIT_ORDER in PKT_CONFG1 for TX and RX, PKT_FIELD_1_CRC_CONFIG for RX. Other applicable properties in the packet handler group still need to be programmed. Field 1 should have the length of 16 bits to contain the PHR with PKT_LEN_FIELD_SOURCE set to 1 for RX. PSDU field shall use Field 2 with variable length. Field 2 length should be set to the maximum allowed including the anticipated FCS length. It is anticipated that the FCS will be calculated by the host and transmitted over the air. PHR and FCS will be put in the FIFO for the host to retrieve and check. Therefore, CRC shouldn't be enabled.

REPLY FIELDS
CTS
  • CTS[7:0]
    • Description: Clear to Send. Indicates that the previous command has completed
      execution and DATA[1..16] is valid. The next command may be sent.
    • Type: U8

GET_PH_STATUS

  • Number: 0x21
  • Summary: Returns the interrupt status of the Packet Handler Interrupt Group (both STATUS and PENDING). Optionally, it may be used to clear latched (PENDING) interrupt events.
  • Purpose:
    • Returns the current interrupt status of Packet Handler interrupt events (both STATUS and PENDING) and optionally clears PENDING interrupts.
    • Please refer to the GET_INT_STATUS command for more details regarding the difference between STATUS and PENDING interrupts.
    • Sending the GET_PH_STATUS command with NO input parameter results in clearing all of the PENDING interrupts.
    • When PENDING interrupts are being cleared, the reply stream reflects their status prior to clearing.
  • Argument Stream:

    • GET_PH_STATUS Argument Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CMD 0x21
    0x01 PH_CLR_PEND FILTER_MATCH_PEND_CLR FILTER_MISS_PEND_CLR PACKET_SENT_PEND_CLR PACKET_RX_PEND_CLR CRC_ERROR_PEND_CLR 0 TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY_PEND_CLR RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL_PEND_CLR

  • Reply Stream:

    • GET_PH_STATUS Reply Stream
    Index Name 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 CTS CTS
    0x01 PH_PEND FILTER_MATCH_PEND FILTER_MISS_PEND PACKET_SENT_PEND PACKET_RX_PEND CRC_ERROR_PEND X TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY_PEND RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL_PEND
    0x02 PH_STATUS FILTER_MATCH FILTER_MISS PACKET_SENT PACKET_RX CRC_ERROR X TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL

PH_CLR_PEND

REPLY FIELDS
CTS
  • CTS[7:0]
    • Description: Clear to Send. Indicates that the previous command has completed
      execution and DATA[1..16] is valid. The next command may be sent.
    • Type: U8
PH_PEND
  • FILTER_MATCH_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the FILTER_MATCH status bit has been detected and therefore a FILTER_MATCH interrupt is pending. See associated FILTER_MATCH status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • FILTER_MISS_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the FILTER_MISS status bit has been detected and therefore a FILTER_MISS interrupt is pending. See associated FILTER_MISS status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • PACKET_SENT_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the PACKET_SENT status bit has been detected and therefore a PACKET_SENT interrupt is pending. See associated PACKET_SENT status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • PACKET_RX_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the PACKET_RX status bit has been detected and therefore a PACKET_RX interrupt is pending. See associated PACKET_RX status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • CRC_ERROR_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the CRC_ERROR status bit has been detected and therefore a CRC_ERROR interrupt is pending. See associated CRC_ERROR status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY status bit has been detected and therefore a TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY interrupt is pending. See associated TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
  • RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL_PEND
    • Description: If set, a rising edge of the RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL status bit has been detected and therefore a RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL interrupt is pending. See associated RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL status bit for more details.
    • Type: U8
PH_STATUS
  • FILTER_MATCH
    • Description: Set to indicate the incoming packet matched filter. Cleared upon entry into RX state, or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • FILTER_MISS
    • Description: Set to indicate the incoming packet was discarded because filter did not match. Cleared upon entry into RX state, or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • PACKET_SENT
    • Description: Set to indicate that data bytes in the TX FIFO were transmitted successfully. Cleared upon entry into TX state.
    • Type: U8
  • PACKET_RX
    • Description: Set to indicate that the expected number of data bytes have been successfully received and placed in the RX FIFO. All enabled Packet Handler functions (e.g., CRC check, Filter Matching) must be successfully completed in order to generate a PACKET_RX interrupt.
    • Type: U8
  • CRC_ERROR
    • Description: Set to indicate that the received CRC checksum byte(s) do not match the calculated CRC checksum value. Cleared upon entry into RX state or if RX is restarted.
    • Type: U8
  • TX_FIFO_ALMOST_EMPTY
    • Description: Set to indicate that the amount of space in the TX FIFO is equal to or greater than the PKT_TX_THRESHOLD value. This interrupt may be used to signal the host MCU to store more data bytes into the TX FIFO, thus providing a means for handling packets with lengths greater than the size of the TX FIFO (i.e., 64 bytes, or 129 bytes in shared FIFO mode). Cleared if the amount of data in the TX FIFO is less than the PKT_TX_THRESHOLD value.
    • Type: U8
  • RX_FIFO_ALMOST_FULL
    • Description: Set to indicate that the number of bytes stored in the RX FIFO is equal to or greater than the PKT_RX_THRESHOLD value. This interrupt may be used to signal the host MCU to read more data bytes from the RX FIFO, thus providing a means for handling packets with lengths greater than the size of the RX FIFO (i.e., 64 bytes, or 129 bytes in shared FIFO mode). Cleared if the amount of data in the RX FIFO is less than the PKT_TX_THRESHOLD value.
    • Type: U8

  • CAL
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high to indicate a RC32K calibration event is pending. If this occurs, the RC32K oscillator will be calibrated on the next transition to Sleep/Standby state.
    • Type: U8
  • FIFO_UNDERFLOW_OVERFLOW_ERROR
    • Description: Set to indicate that the number of received or transmitted bytes exceeds the size of the RX or TX FIFO, respectively (i.e., 64 bytes for each FIFO, or 129 bytes when sharing the FIFO). Upon such an underflow/overflow event, the FIFO(s) will need to be reset. Cleared by issuing a FIFO_INFO command to reset the FIFOs.
    • Type: U8
  • STATE_CHANGE
    • Description: Set to indicate a successful transition from one state to another operating state. Cleared when a state transition is in progress.
    • Type: U8
  • CMD_ERROR
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high to indicate an error has occurred in the processing of a command. For example, an incorrect command/property ID is sent, or an attempt was made to write a property that is outside of the given property group.
    • Type: U8
  • CHIP_READY
    • Description: Set to indicate the chip (upon completion of the POWER_UP sequence) has reached the state where it is ready to accept commands, or when the IR calibration process is completed. Cleared when the chip is shutdown or when IR calibration has begun.
    • Type: U8
  • LOW_BATT
    • Description: Self clearing signal that pulses high to indicate the WUT (Wake-up timer) has expired.
    • Type: U8
  • WUT
    • Description: Set to indicate the battery voltage is below the threshold set by GLOBAL_LOW_BATT_THRESH. Cleared to indicate the battery voltage is above the threshold set by GLOBAL_LOW_BATT_THRESH.
    • Type: U8

    • Format: Enumeration

      • 16 = Bad command issued.
      • 17 = Argment(s) in issued command were invalid.
      • 18 = Command was issued before previous command was completed.
      • 49 = Invalid bootmode supplied.
      • 64 = Bad Property ID was provided.

GLOBAL_XO_TUNE

  • Group: 0x00
  • Index: 0x00
  • Summary: Configure crystal oscillator frequency tuning bank.
  • Purpose:
    • Crystal oscillator frequency tuning value. 0x00 is maximum frequency value and 0x7F is lowest frequency value. Each LSB code corresponds to a 70 fF capacitance change. The total adjustment range assuming a 30 MHz XTAL is +/-100 ppm.
  • Default: 0x40
  • Register View:

    • GLOBAL_XO_TUNE
    Index 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 0 TUNE_VALUE
    Default

      • 127 = Lowest frequency.

GLOBAL_CLK_CFG

  • Group: 0x00

Field Details

    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Divided clock output is disabled.
      • 1 = Divided clock output is enabled.
  • DIVIDED_CLK_SEL[2:0]
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Clock output is system clock divided by 1.
      • 1 = Clock output is system clock divided by 2.
      • 2 = Clock output is system clock divided by 3.
      • 3 = Clock output is system clock divided by 7.5.
      • 4 = Clock output is system clock divided by 10.
      • 5 = Clock output is system clock divided by 15.
      • 6 = Clock output is system clock divided by 30.

      • 1 = 32 kHz clock is driven by internal RC oscillator.

GLOBAL_CONFIG

  • Group: 0x00
  • Index: 0x03
  • Summary: Global configuration settings.
  • Purpose:
    • Various settings that affect entire chip. If PROTOCOL is specified, the chip is placed into protocol aware state.
  • Default: 0x20
  • Register View:

    • GLOBAL_CONFIG
    Index 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x03 0 LPF_SATURATION_MODE SEQUENCER_MODE FIFO_MODE PROTOCOL POWER_MODE
    Default
    0 0x0 0x1 0x0 0x0 0x0

Field Details
  • LPF_SATURATION_MODE
    • Description: This bit determines if the ADC will be put in high power mode when the RSSI level is above MODEM_RSSI_THRESH. If this feature is enabled, the RX current will increase 1 mA if the RSSI is above the threshold.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Enable higher saturation level in LOW_POWER mode.
      • 1 = Lower saturation level (-15 dB), but lower power consumption in LOW_POWER mode.
  • SEQUENCER_MODE
    • Description: This bit determines if the sequencer timing is used, or transmit is started as soon as possible.
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Transmit is guaranteed to occur x us after nSEL goes High. x depends on the current state.
      • 1 = Start TX as soon as possible.
  • FIFO_MODE
    • Description: This bit is effective only when chip power up or after related FIFO reset by sending command FIFO_INFO
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = TX and RX FIFO are independent, 64-byte size for each other.
      • 1 = TX/RX FIFO are sharing with 129-byte size buffer.
  • PROTOCOL[2:0]
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Packet format is generic, no dynamic reprogramming of packet handler properties.
      • 1 = Packet format is IEEE802.15.4g compliant.
  • POWER_MODE
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = High performance mode for RX and TX. RX current = 13 mA.
      • 1 = Low power mode for RX and TX. RX current = 10 mA.

INT_CTL_ENABLE

  • Group: 0x01
  • Index: 0x00
  • Summary: This property provides for global enabling of the three interrupt groups (Chip, Modem and Packet Handler) in order to generate HW interrupts at the NIRQ pin.
  • Purpose:
    • Enables top-level interrupt sources to generate HW interrupts at the NIRQ pin.
    • The three interrupt groups are Chip, Modem and Packet Handler. Each of them contains multiple possible interrupt sources that must be individually enabled via the INT_CTL_PH_ENABLE, INT_CTL_MODEM_ENABLE, INT_CTL_CHIP_ENABLE properties.
    • Note that this property only provides for global enabling/disabling of the HW interrupt indication on the NIRQ output pin. An internal interrupt event may still be generated even if the indication on the NIRQ output pin is disabled. The interrupt event may always be monitored by polling a GPIO pin, or via GET_INT_STATUS, GET_CHIP_STATUS, GET_PH_STATUS, or GET_MODEM_STATUS commands.
  • Default: 0x04
  • Register View:

    • INT_CTL_ENABLE
    Index 7 6 5 4 3 2 1 0
    0x00 0 0 0 0 0 CHIP_INT_STATUS_EN MODEM_INT_STATUS_EN PH_INT_STATUS_EN
    Default
    0 0 0 0 0 0x1 0x0 0x0

Field Details
  • CHIP_INT_STATUS_EN
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Disable pending interrupts in the Chip Status group from asserting nNIRQ.
      • 1 = Enable pending interrupts in the Chip Status group to assert nNIRQ.
  • MODEM_INT_STATUS_EN
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Disable pending interrupts in the Modem group from asserting nNIRQ.
      • 1 = Enable pending interrupts in the Modem group to assert nNIRQ.
  • PH_INT_STATUS_EN
    • Format: Enumeration
      • 0 = Disable pending interrupts in the Packet Handler group from asserting nNIRQ.
      • 1 = Enable pending interrupts in the Packet Handler group to assert nNIRQ.

INT_CTL_PH_ENABLE

  • Group: 0x01
  • Index: 0x01
  • Summary: Enable individual interrupt sources within the Packet Handler Interrupt Group to generate a HW interrupt on the NIRQ output pin.
  • Purpose:
    • Enable individual interrupt sources within the Packet Handler Interrupt Group in order to generate a HW interrupt at the NIRQ output pin.
    • In order to fully enable a HW interrupt, it is necessary to enable both the individual interrupt source (within this property) as well as the corresponding interrupt group (e.g., set INT_CTL_ENABLE:PH_INT_STATUS_EN).
